newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Beirut in sterling, marks and dollar CDs.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Beirut in sterling, marks and dollar CDs.

text.p: Bank of Beirut said on Wednesday it would make two issues of floating-rate certificates of deposit for five million sterling and five million marks next week.

The two-year Deutsche marks CDs to be issued on December 3 bear six-percent interest per annum for the initial six-month period. The remaining undernoted three reset periods are at six month LIBOR plus three percent.
The 12-month sterling CDs to be issued on December 4 carry an initial six-month annual interest of eight percent while the reset period is at six month LIBOR rate fixing plus two percent.

Earlier, the bank announced a $5 million CD issue for December 2. The 18-month issue carries an initial six-month annual interest of 8.25 percent while the remaining two reset periods bear six month LIBOR plus 2.75 percent.
All three issues are exempt from withholding tax.
Bank of Beirut began issuing floating-rate CDs in June 1995 and 12 issues worth the equivalent of $48 million so far have been fully subscribed, with high demand from outside Lebanon.
"There was high foreign demand mainly from the Gulf and some European institutions," Christine Dadour at the bank's treasury and foreign exchange department told Reuters.
Bank of Beirut ranked 17th among Lebanon's 82 banks in 1995 in size of customer deposits.
